title: Cut runner: HotTamale (4 CPUs) stalls the debug build of the release gate; a cut loses an hour for each attempt

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Found at the cut of v0.27.0. The facts are on #3303 (comments of 2026-11-26T00:56Z and 01:26Z).

## What happens

The runner HotTamale took the `camcraft-cut` job of `cut.yml` two times (runs 45727701972 and 45732227750, commit `859dce67c`, branch `release/v0.27.0`). Each time the step `debug build (--no-run)` got a `STALL` row after about 1315 s. There was no `FAIL` row.

- HotTamale reports 4 CPUs, thus the gate uses 4 jobs.
- The debug build of about 1200 test binaries writes no output for more than 15 minutes on 4 CPUs. The watchdog (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN`, 15 minutes) then stops the step.
- The same tree passed on `main` (`9e21ed682`). The third cut run (45735766737) ran on wopr and passed. The v0.26.0 gate passed on wopr with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=24` (debug build 261 s).

Thus a cut can lose about one hour for each attempt on this runner, and the stall is not a defect of the tree.

## The decision is the maintainer's

One of these, or a different choice:

1. HotTamale does not have the `camcraft-cut` label. Only a runner with sufficient CPUs takes a cut job.
2. The watchdog limit for the build step of the release tier is longer, or the build step prints progress, so a slow runner does not stall.
3. `cut.yml` refuses a runner below a CPU count, with a clear message at the start of the job.

No agent changes the runner labels or the limits (`runners` skill). This issue records the facts for the decision.
